claim: AC-2 lets any Plan change build without a dialog once a patch round exists, and the patch round never expires: an agent can rewrite earlier steps or the Route line, or add unrelated steps, and build with no stapel ok.
The Decisions log says a step added to the Plan, but AC-2 and AC-3 test only that the Plan changed; an append-only rule and a test where a changed old step stops the build are missing.
The term Patch round means any code review round, but review::patch_findings counts round 1 only; the round and verdict rule are not stated and no test covers round 2 or the merge round.
AC-6 and AC-7 read Route: light from the current, provisional Plan; an agent on a full tagged ticket writes Route: light and then edits Spec and Design with no dialog until the close.
AC-5 does not say which sections count, what its dialog included means, or that a fully confirmed ticket still closes; existing close tests may break.
AC-11 prints (<exit status>) with no format; a signal kill and a start failure of sh have no text and no test.
The ask for a stapel.toml edit is assumed to reach the person in modes auto and acceptEdits; if Claude Code decides it alone, the agent changes the process keys by itself.
AC-8 covers only case variants of the path; ./, absolute, a/../ and symlink forms of .stapel/stapel.toml are not stated or tested.
The setup's stdin is not stated, and files it makes (node_modules link, .env) make the new worktree dirty, so next prints commit unless the project ignores them.
Frame item 7 says on the base branch, AC-12 says where no ticket of the branch is open; the words differ.
The term Provisional permit says status prints build: provisional, but AC-2 has no status clause.
Plan step 7 is a coverage commit with no RED; its tests pass before any code; step 12 gives no RED reason.
The grant lifetime test does not say how the clock is controlled; a replay of a 24 h grant after the Plan changes has no test named.
Proposal: show provisional sections that wait for stapel ok in stapel status and in the SessionStart output.

note: AC-2 needs an appended Plan (the confirmed Plan text unchanged, new lines after it) and a patch finding in the newest code review round; a changed old line or a round without a patch finding stops the build (AC-3)
the term Appended Plan; the stop cases of an old step changed and of the Route line changed are in next_provisional::fix_steps_build_without_a_dialog
Patch round is the newest whole code-review round (review::finding_round) with a patch finding whose verdict is not false; a round 2 patch and a round 2 without patch are test cases
AC-6 and AC-7 read the route from the Plan text of its last confirmation; a current Plan changed to light stops the build; Not promised line removed
AC-5 counts sections whose owner is not generated, the guard refuses the close dialog before a grant, a fresh ticket closes as today; Design names how fixtures that break go to main
AC-11 status is exit <n>, signal <n> or could not start: <error>; a kill -KILL case is tested, the start failure is in Review Focus

Design decision: the same dialog modes as stapel ok, which showed its dialog in auto mode in STP-32 to STP-35; the builder checks acceptEdits in the hook documentation and stops with intent_gap otherwise; auto is a test case
AC-8 resolves the path as the guard does for every path and compares without case; ./, .., absolute and symlink forms are test cases
AC-10 gives the setup an empty input; files the setup makes are the project's to ignore (Not promised, the skill says so)
Frame item 7 and AC-12 both say where no ticket of the current branch is open
AC-2 prints build: provisional <KEY> when the Plan is in [build] requires; the term says the permit needs a waiting required section
the coverage step is gone: the stop cases live in the tests of AC-2 and AC-6, whose positive cases fail at RED; step 11 names its RED reason; 11 steps
the test compares expires_at with the test's clock plus 86400 s within 5 s; a replayed grant after a change is refused by the existing test ok::refuses_expired_or_mismatched_grant
outside the promise: listed in the Summary for the person to decide at the close or in a later ticket

claim: The Appended Plan term is a character prefix test, so an edit that extends the last confirmed line and adds a new line counts as appended and builds with no stapel ok.
AC-12 does not say what happens when another worktree exists but its ticket or next action cannot be read; one broken worktree can make stapel next and the SessionStart hook fail.
Design does not name the source of the Patch round fact; the existing patch_finding counts round 1 only.
AC-9 gives no order when several refusals apply.
AC-10 and AC-11 do not say whether the worktree: line comes before the setup runs, and Frame item 6 and AC-10 name the output stream differently.
After the step 7 GREEN a subagent edit or an edit in a mode without a dialog gets ask until step 8, so one commit has a weaker guard.

note: Appended Plan compares whole lines: every confirmed line equal and in order, at least one line more; an extended last line is a test case that stops
AC-12: a worktree whose ticket or next action cannot be read gives open: <branch> — <path> — next: unreadable and the rest of the output stays; a corrupt state.json is a test case
Design: the patch round is a new fact from review::finding_round; patch_finding stays for next_round
AC-9 judges the refusals in the order subagent, mode, apply, load
AC-10: the worktree: line first, then the setup with its stdout and stderr on stderr, then setup: ok; Frame item 6 says the same
step 7 asks only for the main agent in a dialog mode with a result that loads; every other case keeps today's denial until step 8

claim: next::decide prints the fact line provisional: plan waits for stapel ok <KEY> before the close whenever provisional() holds, also at level close when nothing waits, and names the Plan when Spec, Design or Proof is the waiting section.

stage::level_close makes every waiting section other than the Description provisional; a custom section of [build] requires also builds on the provisional permit, while AC-6 names only Spec, Design, Proof and Plan.
AC-10 quotes the load error worktree.setup is empty, while config.rs prints worktree.setup is empty: name a shell command.

AC-7: a waiting section other than Spec, Design, Proof and Plan keeps level close as all; Plan step 13
